name: Матовий майстер: лінійний мат (2)
description:
Now that you have mastered the rook and queen lawmower mate, it is time for a new monster trick: the lawnmower mate with two rooks!

Study examples 1 and 2 to learn how to do set up this mate.

Example 1 shows how the king is mated in het end.
Example 2 explains how to get there step-by-step.

A lawnmower mate with two rooks is very similar to the lawnmower mate with a queen and a rook. Yet, there is one important difference.

Have a look at example 3.

With two rooks, you need to be careful. If the king is close to the rooks, checking the king is not a good idea. To make the lawnmower mate work, you may have to move the rook(s) away from the king. 

Example 4 explains this.

 

What do you have to do?

Deliver a lawnmower mate. Alternate between the rooks and roll back the black king. Gradually cut off all escape paths.
Make sure the king cannot take your rooks. Simply transfer them to the other side of the board if the king is close.

examples.text:
One rook dominates the 7th rank. The other checks the king on the eighth.
The rooks cut off the escape paths on their rows (see green arrows): checkmate!

examples.pgn: {[%csl Re5,Rf5,Rg5][%cal Gb5h5]} 1. Ra6+ Ke7 2. Rb7+ Kd8 3. Ra8# 1-0
examples.text:
The rook on the 5th rank stops the king from moving down (see green arrows and red squares). It does a good job here.
Now, White is going to take away more escape squares. He brings in the 4th-rank rook to do that. It moves to the 6th rank.
Black is in check. The king must step back.

Now the rook on the 6th rank is positioned perfectly, fending off the king on the 6th rank.
Time for the 5th-rank rook to come and help. It checks the king on the 7th rank, pushing the king to the edge of the board.

The other rook finishes the job: it checkmates the king on the 8th rank.

Do you recognise this position? It is the mating pattern from example 1. Checkmate!

In this position, the king is closer to the white rooks than in examples 1 and 2.
That is a good thing for Black. He can simply get out of check by capturing the rook on the 7th rank! 
Had the other rook been a queen, Black could not have done this. For the rook would have been defended by the queen.

White can almost deliver the final mate blow with one of his rooks.
He just has to take care that the black king cannot capture his rooks.
That's why he moves the 7th-rank rook to one of the green squares first.
In the next move, this rook can check the king on the 8th rank.
